US Census proposal aims to exclude non-citizens

The Trump administration has proposed significant changes to the U.S. Census, aiming to exclude non-citizens from the count. This overhaul could reshape voting maps and alter the representation of states in the House of Representatives. The proposed changes would stop asking about race and exclude millions of U.S. residents from the census count, which the 14th Amendment mandates include the "whole number of persons in each state." The administration's proposal seeks to change who is considered to be living in America for census purposes.
